timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Traveling has been my life learning about new food and new cultures.
In my pond of Trisha we were going to go to California and are going to eat all up and down the coast to learn about the local food scene there.
And then 2020 happens and you know everything got derailed.
I'm Ed Shameinsky, I'm the chef and owner of Dame or seafood restaurant in the Greenwich Village.
I'm from London originally. My father was an academic.
He would teach at different universities all across the world.
The exposure of such a young child to all these different cultures, the different cuisines, the smells, really defined my view of food and it informs my cooking to this day.
Turbo is my favourite fish in the world, it's the King of the Sea.
It's a show-stopping centrepiece of every table at Dame.
We season it and grill it whole, put it on this big vintage serving platter and then set it on fire as it goes out to the table and everyone looks around and say, what's that?
It's a really joyful eating experience.
But then 2020 happened and we couldn't get them.
You know last year it was really difficult to get the quality of ingredients that we needed.
So we had to change and adapt the restaurant.
We thought well how can we do something that is true to ourselves and also give back to, you know, our community.
We started the pop-up just cooking fish and chips.
We donated all of our profits, $20,000 to fight racial inequality.
It was a difficult time to operate a restaurant, but it was a beautiful time to build a community.
What I'm most looking forward to is getting back out there and seeing the world.
And because of Delta we can travel again.
The first thing I'm going to do is go to the West Coast and take that trip that I've been thinking about for years.
For me traveling is about people and it's about the moments I get to share with those people.
I miss having a cup of tea, my grandmother's house in London or it's having a pint at the pub.
Because all of those are the things that really brought in my horizons and make me grow as an individual.
I guess I didn't realise how much I missed that until it was gone.
The future is really, really exciting for me.
I can cook my turban again.

youtube_description:
Ed Szymanski usually finds inspiration for his Greenwich Village restaurant through travel. But after putting his bucket-list trip to the West Coast on hold last year, the chef had to get creative, turning his attention to giving back to his community.

Hear how the experience reinvigorated his love of travel and learn more about how @Delta Air Lines is helping Ed find culinary inspiration once again in this episode of Creator Connections.
